returnedFinding.attackerControl: Reference DOCX bytes supplied to an application or conversion workflow accepting untrusted templates.
returnedFinding.body: A caller-supplied reference DOCX is opened with PartFs::open and its main XML is passed into frame/final_section without package admission or checked XML parsing. PartFs bounds ZIP sizes and entry counts but does not enforce XML depth on document parts. final_section calls the explicitly unchecked Dom::parse_xdocument, whose parse_element recursively descends for every nested element without a depth limit. Consequently, a deeply nested reference document can exhaust the native Python/Rust process stack or trap the WASM instance despite the advertised max_xml_depth=256 policy. This is reachable through Rust markdown_to_docx, Python from_markdown(reference=...), WASM markdownToDocx(..., reference), and CLI --reference-doc conversion paths.
counterevidenceAndLimits: ZIP compressed-size, entry-count and inflation budgets still apply through PartFs::open; this finding concerns the missing XML-depth gate.
Normal inspection/edit paths perform admission before parsing and are not implicated by this reference-specific trace.
No public deployment, authenticated tenant boundary or universal remote reachability is assumed.
No triggering input was created and no application code was executed; stack threshold and precise platform failure behavior were not measured.
prerequisites: The application accepts an attacker-supplied reference document rather than selecting exclusively trusted templates.
The application does not independently admit/check the reference before conversion.
returnedFinding.protectedAsset: Availability of the embedding Python/Rust process, conversion worker or WASM instance.
returnedFinding.remediation: Admit the caller-supplied reference with the selected InputLimits before any reference XML reaches unchecked DOM parsing, including the main document and preserved auxiliary parts. Alternatively, make each reference consumer use checked parsing with the same explicit limits; preserve malformed-document errors rather than silently weakening policy.

returnedFinding.attacker: A caller supplying an untrusted legacy DOC piece table.
returnedFinding.controls_and_counterevidence: Checked arithmetic and word.get/u16_at refuse physical offsets outside WordDocument. Increasing CP validation prevents backwards logical pieces. returnedFinding.impact: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering.
returnedFinding.invariant: A physically bounded OLE file must not materialize an unrestricted logical character sequence through repeated references to the same bytes.

locations.evidence: ccp_text is read directly as an attacker-controlled u32.

returnedFinding.remediation: Introduce a configurable legacy logical-character/output budget and check ccp_text and cumulative decoded characters before materialization. Bound retained metadata independently of physical stream size.
returnedFinding.rule: Bound logical story expansion before materializing characters

returnedFinding.impact: A false EOCD carrying count zero and inconsistent disk fields can be placed inside the real EOCD comment. returnedFinding.invariant: The entry count checked before indexing must describe the central directory subsequently opened.

locations.evidence: preindex_budget trusts declared_entry_count for the max_entries decision.

returnedFinding.remediation: Resolve and validate the selected EOCD consistently with the ZIP reader before applying preindex limits. Independently reject archive.len() above max_entries after opening, and obtain the selected raw central-record count for exact-duplicate detection.
returnedFinding.rule: Budget the same central directory the ZIP reader actually selects

surfaces.label: Tolerated XML syntax can hide recursive elements from admission
surfaces.notes: For the unquoted/comment route, `<r a=x><!-- x>` followed by nested tags and a comment close is a shallow root/comment sequence to admission; raw parse_element treats the first x as a quote and the x inside the comment as its close. It then reaches the nested tags without recognizing the comment opener it already consumed. No later depth guard exists before recursive parse_element. A DTD internal entity literal containing nested tags similarly falls under ignored DocType events but the raw skip consumes only the first >. These are grammar interpretation issues, not external-entity fetching. Strict validate_xml uses quoted attributes and explicitly refuses DTDs, but rendering's package-admission path does not invoke that strict gate.

surfaces.label: Non-XML auxiliary filenames bypass admission before recursive parsing
surfaces.notes: Admission identifies XML by filename rather than all actual XML consumers. Relationship-selected auxiliary parts are subsequently passed to the permissive recursive DOM parser without the active XML depth/tag gate. Counterevidence: The main document's alternate extension is explicitly checked. ZIP inflation, CRC and entry budgets remain active. Raw parse_xdocument is intentionally unchecked; the bug is the admitted-package path missing the promised preceding gate. Inspect parse_part_within independently validates its selected XML.

surfaces.label: Decoded relationship ampersands trigger quadratic target resolution
surfaces.notes: An already decoded relationship target is decoded twice, and the permissive entity helper rescans the full remaining suffix after every unsuccessful ampersand. Counterevidence: Raw repeated ampersands in XML do not pass quick-xml admission; this path uses valid escaped references. External relationships are filtered by cited consumers, but an internal relationship suffices. Locked local oxml-opc 0.14.2 relationship.rs:924-940 uses decoded_and_normalized_value; src/opc/mod.rs:1222-1248 tests decoded values. The comment claiming raw attributes at :678 is contradicted by implementation.

surfaces.label: Identical duplicate relationship repair performs quadratic scans
surfaces.notes: The duplicate detector uses a HashMap but separately tracks already repaired IDs in a growing Vec searched with contains for every identical duplicate. Counterevidence: Conflicting duplicate records are refused immediately. ZIP entry-count caps do not cap relationship count inside a single part. Repeating one ID alone does not create the growing-vector worst case; the distinct-ID sequence does.

surfaces.label: Intern-pool saturation duplicates long namespace URIs per element
surfaces.notes: The count-bounded global string pool falls back to Arc::from for every new string when saturated. Active namespace URIs are re-interned for each XName rather than sharing the parser scope's allocation, so bounded declarations are multiplied by element count. Previously interned URIs continue sharing allocation. Depth, URI-length and cumulative declaration budgets are real, but charge declarations rather than repeated expanded-name storage. The thread-local pool remains filled across subsequent documents; process limits contain impact.

surfaces.label: Markdown XML tree duplicates inherited namespace maps for each child declaration
surfaces.notes: Each Element retains Arc<HashMap<String,String>>. element_from clones its parent's Arc then calls Arc::make_mut to add a namespace, which deep-clones all inherited String values for that child; previous children retain their copies. Children with no declarations share the Arc and are not the demonstrated case. 64 root bindings plus one child binding is within 256 live bindings; approximately 256KiB root declaration bytes plus 120KiB repeated small declarations is below the 1MiB declaration budget. The independent xmllinq parser's scoped-overlay implementation does not protect this separate Markdown tree.

surfaces.label: Markdown reference DOCX reaches recursive XML parsing before admission
surfaces.notes: The optional reference document is treated as ready for raw DOM construction after PartFs::open, whose byte/metadata checks do not perform general XML depth validation. ZIP byte/entry/inflation budgets remain enforced. Ordinary primary-document entrypoints admit their inputs; that control is absent on this optional reference path. Raw XML parsing is intentionally permissive; the missing preceding admission on a byte API is the defect. Exact platform stack exhaustion depth was not measured.

surfaces.label: Tracked-edit audit parses permission-bearing XML before admission
surfaces.notes: Security-relevant XML parsing occurs in the permission precheck before admission; the later reject_changes refusal cannot protect earlier recursive DOM construction. Without the original permission substring this particular preparse is skipped. ZIP budgets still apply. Later admission exists but follows the sensitive operation. The result is process DoS; no privilege or external service is assumed.

surfaces.label: Python CLI output writes follow substituted symlinks
surfaces.notes: The existence check is not bound to the later truncating pathname open; the final write follows symlinks. Preconditions: Output directory entries can be created/replaced by an independently lower-trust local actor. Redirected file is writable by victim but not attacker; platform permits the relevant symlink traversal.

surfaces.label: npm CLI output writes follow substituted symlinks
surfaces.notes: The check follows links and does not bind the subsequently opened object; default writeFileSync truncates and follows symlinks. Preconditions: Output directory is independently writable by a lower-trust local principal. Victim can write the redirected target and attacker cannot; platform/kernel symlink protections permit the chosen setup.

surfaces.label: Python plan recording follows predictable temporary-file symlinks
surfaces.notes: A predictable staging pathname is opened with ordinary truncating writes instead of exclusive, no-follow creation within private staging. Preconditions: Victim records a plan in a directory independently writable by a lower-trust local principal. Attacker knows/predicts basename and process ID and can pre-place a permitted symlink to a victim-only writable target.

surfaces.label: npm plan recording follows predictable temporary-file symlinks
surfaces.notes: The PID-based staging name is not exclusively created, so the initial staging write can follow an attacker-prepared link. Preconditions: Victim plan directory is independently writable by a lower-trust local actor. Attacker predicts PID/basename and the platform permits following the prepared symlink to a victim-writable target.

surfaces.label: A shared font-index parent permits symlink-directed cache staging writes
surfaces.notes: Font-index staging derives its name from PID and opens it without exclusive creation or a no-follow policy. The relevant authority is the effective index parent, not the configured fonts directory. Preconditions: Operator sets a supported index/font-directory configuration whose effective cache parent is independently writable by a lower-trust actor. Attacker predicts PID/temp basename; target is victim-writable but not directly attacker-writable. Relevant platform symlink protections allow that shared-parent setup.
